title: Mr. Keen, Tracer of Lost Persons
paragraphs: A long-running detective drama about the kindly but persistent Mr. Keen, a professional tracer who searches for missing people and becomes involved in mysteries surrounding their disappearances.

Long-running Hummert detective property derived from Robert W. Chambers’ 1906 The Tracer of Lost Persons. Early surviving GRH material preserves multi-part tracer stories; later surviving broadcasts are predominantly half-hour standalone murder and mystery cases. The 63 broadcast objects in GRH are a small survival subset of a much larger original run.
GRH documents the program through Early tracer / serial era (October 12, 1937 to December 31, 1943) and Half-hour case era in surviving archive (January 6, 1944 to April 19, 1955).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Anne Hummert (producer on 50 recordings, creator on 26 recordings, writer on 17 recordings, and author on 2 recordings), Frank Hummert (producer on 50 recordings, creator on 26 recordings, writer on 6 recordings, performer on 2 recordings, and dialogue writer on 1 recording), [[person|bennett-kilpack|Bennett Kilpack]] (performer on 40 recordings), Larry Elliott (announcer on 26 recordings), Lawrence Klee (dialogue writer on 19 recordings, performer on 19 recordings, and writer on 1 recording), Phillip Clarke (performer on 12 recordings), and Richard Leonard (director on 8 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and homicide, family, marriage and domestic conflict, missing persons and disappearances, inheritance, wealth and family property, kidnapping and unlawful confinement, and wartime industry, sabotage and national defense.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Whitehall and rotating sponsor commercial-radio model, Wartime domestic-security story context, Serial-to-standalone detective format evolution, and Extreme survival scarcity from a long-running radio property.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|the-big-show|The Big Show]] (3 shared credited people), [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (2 shared credited people), [[show|dragnet|Dragnet]] (2 shared credited people), [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]] (2 shared credited people), and [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]] (2 shared credited people).
